method.indices: Takahashi et al. (2011) E and C: EOF1/EOF2 of monthly SST anomalies, here 10°S–10°N, 140°E–80°W (Takahashi et al. used HadISST from coast to coast); E = (PC1 − PC2)/√2, C = (PC1 + PC2)/√2, in standard deviations
method.obs: NOAA ERSSTv6 monthly, 2° grid, fixed 1991–2020 base, no detrending
method.forecast: C3S seasonal-postprocessed-single-levels, member SST anomalies vs each model's own 1993–2016 hindcast, moved onto the 1991–2020 base with the observed climatology difference, projected at the ERSST 2° points
method.classes: east-based: E − C ≥ 1; central: E − C ≤ −1; basin-wide between
method.centre: anomaly-weighted mean longitude of the 2°S–2°N anomaly (10° running mean) where it is within 30% of its peak, searched 150°E–80°W
method.verdict_rule: a class is named only when the across-model t-test of E − C against 0 gives p < 0.05, two thirds of the members (each model weighted equally) fall in the class, and all but at most one model mean does; a significant lean that misses the other two is reported as a lean; anything else as a split
method.trend_note: On the fixed base the western Pacific's faster warming puts a slow drift into C (see trend_per_decade); E barely moves. Older events therefore sit slightly low on C.

excluded_note: excluded for poor ENSO skill and drift

hindcast.text: Tested on the models' own October hindcasts, 1993–2016 (24 years, 5 systems: ECMWF SEAS5, UKMO GloSea6, Météo-France 9, NCEP CFSv2, ECCC CanSIPSv3): the share of a model's first-month error in C that is still there later (pooled, fitted with each year left out) is 0.88 in Oct–Dec, 0.72 in Nov–Jan, 0.55 in Dec–Feb; in E it is 0.90, 0.69, 0.39. The correction applies those weights. Out of sample it changes the multi-model error in E − C in Nov–Jan from 0.62 to 0.59, which is not statistically significant (Wilcoxon over years, p = 0.3). In 1997, the strongest east-based event in the hindcast period, the models' average for Oct–Dec had E +3.9 and C +1.0 against an observed E +4.2 and C +0.3: too central, the same direction as this year's first-month error. A regression calibration of E and C on the hindcasts does not beat the forecast as issued (0.56 in Nov–Jan).
hindcast.rule: first-month-corrected leads only if, in the hindcasts, it lowers the multi-model E − C error at the peak season with p < 0.05 (Wilcoxon over years) and raises it in no season

ttest.test: one-sample t-test of the model-mean E − C against 0, each model once
